remotes.title: Magic Remote MR25GA
sources: OLED48C56LB, webOS 10.3.0, 17 November 2026: CH+ and CH- received by the key filter

OLED48C56LB, webOS 10.3.0, 21 November 2026: every key but Power pressed and read from the remote's input device (LGE M-RCU - Builtin [0]): Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, LG Channels, Alexa, the key in Sling TV's place (sent as IR_KEY_RAKUTENTV), CH+ and CH-, Guide, the house in a circle (IR_KEY_INPUT_HUB), ? (IR_KEY_MULTIKEY, held as the same code), 123 (IR_KEY_SCREEN_REMOTE), and the AI key (RF_KEY_VOICE, the microphone's code); also Home, Back, Settings, the arrows, the wheel and volume, which the Remote tab does not offer
OLED48C56LB, webOS 10.3.0, 22 November 2026: the TV reports the remote as LGE MR25GA in its Bluetooth device list, its pairing file and lginput2's press log; the remote's label says MR25GA
The AI key as its own key (ai) is from webOS 11's native mapping; on webOS 10 it arrives as the microphone key (voice), so the Remote tab names that key AI for this remote
No number keys, no red, green, yellow or blue keys, and no Info or Input key
123 (screenremote) was pressed on 21 November 2026 above but left out until the Remote tab offered it (#1709)
remotes.notes: Every button on the remote was pressed except Power, and the owner confirmed on 22 November 2026 that the list is every button it has.

remotes.title: Magic Remote MR23
sources: OLED48C31LA, webOS 11.2.0, 25 November 2026: the remote paired with the TV, reported by the TV as LGE MR23, read from lginput2's NL_BUTTON_CLICK and NL_NON_LIST_BUTTON_CLICK lines in /var/log/messages, pressed one at a time: Netflix (KEY_NETFLIX), Prime Video (KEY_AMAZON), Disney+ (KEY_DISNEY), LG Channels (KEY_LGCHANNELS), Rakuten TV (KEY_RAKUTEN), Alexa (KEY_ALEXAVOICE), channel up and down (KEY_CHANNELUP, KEY_CHANNELDOWN), Guide (KEY_GUIDE), the microphone (KEY_VOICE), Input (KEY_INPUT), the … button under which AD/SAP is printed (KEY_SCREEN_REMOTE), a number key (KEY_5) and Red (KEY_RED); also Home (KEY_HOME, not Home Hub), Back (KEY_PREVIOUS) and OK, which the Remote tab does not offer

The owner confirmed on 25 November 2026 that the remote has no Home Hub (house in a circle) button, no ? button, no Apps, Movies or Info key, and that green, yellow and blue are printed beside the measured Red key
As for the MR25GA: the microphone arrives as the AI key (ai) on webOS 11's native mapping, which does not depend on the remote's model, rather than the microphone key (voice) that lginput2 logs
remotes.notes: Every Remote tab key the owner could identify was pressed and read from the log; green, yellow and blue were not pressed individually, assumed from Red and the owner's own account of the remote's layout.

remotes.title: Magic Remote MR22N
sources: OLED42C24LA, webOS 9.2.2, 27 November 2026: the remote paired with the TV, reported by the TV as LGE MR22N, every button but Power pressed one at a time by the owner and read both as Linux key codes from the TV's input devices and from lginput2's button_type lines in /var/log/messages: the number keys 1 to 9 and 0 (KEY_1 to KEY_0), Guide (KEY_GUIDE, Linux 362), the … button (KEY_SCREEN_REMOTE, 994), volume up and down and mute, channel up and down (KEY_CHANNELUP, KEY_CHANNELDOWN), the arrows, Back (KEY_PREVIOUS), Settings (KEY_SETTINGS), Red, Green, Yellow and Blue, Netflix (KEY_NETFLIX), Prime Video (KEY_AMAZON), Disney+ (KEY_DISNEY), Rakuten TV (KEY_RAKUTEN), Google Assistant (KEY_GOOGLEVOICE) and Alexa (KEY_ALEXAVOICE)
The owner confirmed the remote also has Home, Input, the microphone and OK on the wheel, which were not read; Home, Back, Settings and OK are not keys the Remote tab offers
remotes.notes: Every button was pressed and read except Power, Home, Input, the microphone and OK; Input and the microphone are listed from the owner's account.

remotes.title: Magic Remote MR20
sources: OLED48CX8LC, webOS 5.6.2, 25 November 2026: the remote already paired with the TV, reported by the TV as LGE MR20, read from lginput2's NL_BUTTON_CLICK lines in /var/log/messages, pressed one at a time: Netflix (KEY_NETFLIX), Prime Video (KEY_AMAZON), Movies (KEY_MOVIES), the microphone (KEY_VOICE), Guide (KEY_GUIDE), Input (KEY_INPUT), a number key (KEY_1); also Home and the dash-marked key that opens LG's own Live Menu (KEY_DASH, which the Remote tab does not offer), which the Remote tab does not offer
The … button opened com.webos.app.screenremote, the Remote tab's 123 button key, though its own NL_BUTTON_CLICK line was not caught
Channel up and down were not read from the log on this webOS version, but the owner confirmed they move the Guide's screens

The owner confirmed the remote has no Disney+, LG Channels, Rakuten TV, Alexa, Home Hub (house in a circle), ? button, Apps or Info key, has colour keys (not pressed individually, assumed from LG's usual four), and has Play, Pause and a List key, which the Remote tab does not offer
remotes.notes: Every Remote tab key the owner could identify was pressed and read from the log, except channel up and down (confirmed by what they do instead) and the colour keys (assumed, universal on LG remotes).

remotes.title: Magic Remote MR18
sources: 49SK8500PLA, webOS 4.4.3, 26 November 2026: the remote already paired with the TV, reported by the TV as LGE MR18, read from lginput2's NL_BUTTON_CLICK lines in /var/log/messages, pressed one at a time: Netflix (KEY_NETFLIX), Prime Video (KEY_AMAZON) and the microphone (KEY_VOICE)

Guide opened Glasshouse Home's guide and Input opened com.tvweb.inputbar, read from the SAM launch lines, not a button_type line; a number key opened LG's own remoteUserList (Quick Access) overlay, read the same way
The owner confirmed channel up and down are handled; not read from the log, since this TV has no tuned channels and Live TV opens LG Channels instead

The owner confirmed the remote has List, Guide, AD, Netflix, Prime Video, Text, T.Opt, Live Zoom, colour keys, Input and a microphone, and that it has no Home Hub (house in a circle), ? button, Movies, Info or Apps key; List, AD, Text, T.Opt and Live Zoom are not keys the Remote tab offers
Colour keys are offered on this webOS version through the existing filter-based Remote tab mechanism (action 'lg' by default), independent of this entry; not pressed individually

OLED65B8SLC (webOS 4.4.3), 27 November 2026: the owner pressed, by faded labels, the two buttons at the bottom (LG answered each with 'This function is not available'), AD and Live Zoom, read as Linux key codes from the TV's input devices: 779 and 780 (IR_KEY_TELETEXT and IR_KEY_TEXTOPTION in LG's key table, Text and T.Opt), 994 (IR_KEY_SCREEN_REMOTE), pressed as AD, and 1027 (IR_KEY_LIVE_ZOOM). Whether AD sends 994 or another button was pressed is not settled, so AD is not listed. On the MR23 the … button, which sends the same key, has AD/SAP printed under it, so the MR18's AD button may well be that key
remotes.notes: Netflix, Prime Video and the microphone were read as button_type lines; Guide, Input and the number keys were confirmed by what they opened instead, since webOS 4.4.3 does not log them as streaming-button clicks. Channel up and down were confirmed by the owner rather than read. Colour keys are assumed present and already configurable on this webOS version regardless of the remote's catalogue entry.
